findings.explanation: Splunkbase 5380 is 'Mattermost Alerts'. The Splunk Add-on for VMware is 3215, and its documented sourcetypes are vmware:perf:<counter-group>, vmware:inv:hostsystem, and vmware:events. Neither vmware:perf nor vmware:vc:event exists, and ESXi version and build live in host inventory, not perf data. The same error repeats in app, references, and detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: Secondary: Splunk Add-on for VMware vSphere ([Splunkbase 5380](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/5380)) to `index=vmware` (or a named metrics index) with `sourcetype=vmware:perf` for ESXi `product_version` / build-style fields
findings.suggested_fix: Cite Splunk Add-on for VMware (3215). Take the ESXi build from vmware:inv:hostsystem and vCenter events from vmware:events.

findings.explanation: In the VxRail API, system/initialize is the Day-1 cluster deployment call, not an authentication step, so telling a poller to POST it is dangerous. X-Vxm-Token is not a documented header, and GET /rest/vxm/v1/lcm, /lcm/history, and /supportability/status also need confirming; the running version is normally read from GET /rest/vxm/v1/system.
findings.quote: session cookie after `POST /rest/vxm/v1/system/initialize` in others, or a vendor header such as `X-Vxm-Token`
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Dell VxRail API reference for your release, remove system/initialize from the auth guidance, and list only documented GET paths and their auth model.

findings.explanation: 'VxRay' appears many times (VxRay Manager, VxRay Software, VxRay LCM, VxRay case), including in exclusions. The product is VxRail.

The description and controlTest present null guards (release_date_epoch > 0, is_supported_until_epoch > 0) as alert conditions. The real ladder is: critical for out-of-support bundles or a Failed LCM state, high for mixed ESXi versions or an n-minus breach, medium for bundles older than 365 days, and low for precheck flags or recent history failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate the sev0 ladder in the description and controlTest.

findings.explanation: UC-19.1.x is the Cisco UCS subcategory. Resync and rebuild progress for HCI lives in UC-19.2.9 and UC-19.2.30 according to the sibling list, so UC-19.1.48 looks like a wrong cross-reference.
findings.quote: remain UC-19.2.13, UC-19.1.48, and related storage-health UCs
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm what UC-19.1.48 covers and, if appropriate, point to UC-19.2.9 and UC-19.2.30 instead.

findings.explanation: Asterisk (the PBX), snmp, and snmp_ups have nothing to do with VxRail LCM compliance. These tags will mis-route equipment filters.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep vxrail, dell_emc, hardware_bmc, and vmware, and drop asterisk, snmp, and snmp_ups.

findings.explanation: The HEC link is truncated to a directory, and the Dell link is a generic manuals hub rather than the VxRail API reference the UC depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the HEC page (Data/UsetheHTTPEventCollector) and the Dell VxRail API reference guide.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified, yet its add-on ID points at an unrelated app, its sourcetypes do not exist, and its SPL does not parse, so no SME verification is evident.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade the status until the poller paths and the SPL have been validated against a VxRail Manager.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Every multisearch arm ends with `stats ... by cluster_id`. multisearch accepts only purely streaming subsearches, so the search fails. Move the per-arm aggregation after the union, or use append or union.

The arm that searches sourcetype="vmware:perf" for os_version or product_version will match nothing, because the VMware add-on emits vmware:perf:* and vmware:inv:hostsystem, and perf data carries no product version.

The third `join type=left max=0 [ ... | fields + ga_seq ]` has no join field and no field in common with the main results, so how ga_seq is attached is unclear. Use appendcols, or eval a constant key on both sides.

summary: The VxRail lifecycle (LCM) bundle-compliance idea is well explained, including CVS bundle semantics, governance lookups, and freeze demotion. But the VMware add-on ID and sourcetypes are wrong, several VxRail Manager REST paths look invented, and one of them is a Day-1 initialisation call misused for authentication. The SPL also places stats inside multisearch arms, which Splunk rejects.
